title: Coagulation analysis with ROTEM sigma versus ROTEM delta in liver transplantation
summary:
The aim of this non-interventional, single-centre study is to investigate whether viscoelastic coagulation analysis using the ROTEM sigma device in liver transplantation provides similar results to those obtained with the ROTEM delta device. For this purpose, up to six blood samples will be routinely analysed with the ROTEM delta device during surgery. At the same time, an additional blood sample (5.4 ml of citrated blood) is taken at each measurement time and analysed with the ROTEM sigma device. The results of both methods are recorded anonymously and compared statistically.
All adult patients who have received a liver transplant at the University Hospital Essen and who have given their consent are eligible to participate. Women of childbearing age who are not using contraception can also participate, as the study is non-invasive and carries no medical risks. Recruitment is done through the Anaesthesia Clinic, who will inform the study physicians, who will inform the patients and obtain written consent. Alternatively, this can be done by the anaesthetist performing the procedure. It is planned to recruit 100 patients.
Statistical analysis will include tests for normal distribution, Spearman correlation, Bland-Altman plots and linear regression. The data will be kept anonymous for ten years and will only be available to the study doctors.
In addition, it will be investigated whether FXIII deficiency can be detected with the viscoelastic tests and what clinical significance such a deficiency has for patients after liver transplantation, both immediately (transfusion requirement) and in the medium term (wound healing disorders).
conditions: All patients are eligible for liver transplantation, including whole organ transplantation, split liver transplantation and retransplantation.

interventions.name: It is a monocentric, non-interventional, clinical obeservation study in the context of liver transplantation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All consenting adult patients undergoing liver transplantation at the University Hospital Essen will be included. Although this includes women of childbearing potential who are not using contraception, a medical implication is excluded as this is a non-interventional study.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent in patients who are minors.
